name: Zala Z-16

placement_rationale.text: 6 km is the Zala Z-16 crew's launch/control depth, not the 75 km comms range its own characteristics report. Like the Supercam S350 it's paired with in this catalog, it sits one notch deeper than the Orlan-10's 4 km — just past doctrine.md §2's 1–5 km close-reconnaissance band but well inside the drone-dense corridor (~30 km either side of the front) — plausible for a small electric reconnaissance type flown persistently rather than for a single high-value sortie, per this asset's own employment_notes on multi-day pattern-of-life mapping. (Nudged 6→6.4 km from this category's shared round-number value so it doesn't literally coincide with side_b-uav-supercam-s350 on the map's distance axis — a small, deterministic spread within the same band, not a new plausibility claim beyond what's already argued above.)

characteristics: Strength: Electric propulsion (quieter than internal-combustion types like Orlan-10); has active evasion mechanisms against counter-drone systems
Limitation: Shorter comms range and lower speed than larger reconnaissance types like Orlan-10 or Supercam
Estimated quantity available: Fleet size not disclosed
employment_notes: Part of the large Zala family (multiple numbered variants cataloged) reflecting Russia's iterative, many-variant approach to tactical drone development
contrast_vs_traditional: A small tactical reconnaissance UAV doing the same job traditional doctrine assigned to a forward observer or a manned spotter aircraft — except cheaply enough to fly constantly rather than occasionally, which is what makes the doctrine.md finding on multi-day pattern-of-life detection possible in the first place: persistent low-cost overwatch, not a single flight, is what maps a sector.
